desc: Finalize algorithm design: verify the segment-tree-over-j-positions with sorted-vectors + batched-lazy-push scheme (updates add min(v,B_j) globally; queries are position-prefix sums; process queries sorted by X) computes M(X,Y)=Σ_{i≤X}Σ_{j≤Y}min(A_i,B_j) correctly; confirm Ans = Y·SA_X + X·SB_Y − 2M; hand-check sample 1 (done: gives 6 ✓); confirm batched-push complexity O(N log N) with two-pointer sweeps and write precise node data layout.

Implement: build segment tree over j with sorted B values + prefix sums per node; iterative update(v) applying to root lazy; push(node) batches pending updates to children with two-pointer O(|L|+size); prefix query [1,Y] with pushes; main loop: sort queries by X, sweep i=1..N applying update(A_i), answer M, combine Ans = Y·SA_X + X·SB_Y − 2M; fast I/O (sys.stdin.buffer).

Write brute-force reference (O(X·Y) per query) and randomized self-test comparing both on small N,K (run locally in reasoning, fix discrepancies, especially min/equality handling and 64-bit overflow — Python ints fine).

Consider simpler alternative before coding: double-check whether a Fenwick-over-values sweep processing queries sorted by X with a SECOND Fenwick over j-positions can achieve O((N+K) log N) (re-derive Σ_{j≤Y}[B_j·cntA_X(≥B_j) + sumA_X(<B_j)] as a single pass where inserting A_i=v does Fenwick range-adds on value-sorted-j and queries use position order — if a clean O((N+K) log N) 2-BIT solution exists, prefer it over the segment tree).
